distribution.title:
The purpose of data collection and generation in the U-TEST project is to develop and analytically validate a non-invasive, urine-based diagnostic approach for early detection of neonatal bacterial sepsis, advancing the technology readiness level from TRL 3 to TRL 4.
Data will be generated to:
• Optimize and validate a dried urine spot (DUS) sample collection protocol suitable for neonatal clinical settings;
• Quantify a predefined panel of urinary metabolite biomarkers using a targeted LC–MS workflow;
• Evaluate the diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, AUC, reproducibility) of the biomarker-based model in both retrospective and prospective neonatal cohorts;
• Support refinement of statistical and machine learning–based diagnostic models.
The data originate from:
• Clinical urine samples collected from neonates admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) at the Children’s Clinical University Hospital (BKUS);
• Existing biobank samples from previous ethically approved studies;
• Experimental LC–MS measurements and derived analytical outputs generated at Riga Technical University (RTU).
All data collection and processing directly support the project’s scientific, clinical validation, and commercialization objectives.

dataset.title: A urine-based diagnostic for the detection of sepsis biomarkers in infants

dmp.description: The main objective of the U-TEST project is to develop and validate a non-invasive urine-based diagnostic test for the early detection of neonatal bacterial sepsis. The innovation builds upon our previous work on urinary metabolite profiling to provide a safer, repeatable alternative to traditional blood-based diagnostics, reducing the need for invasive procedures in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs).
dmp.ethical_issues_description: The project involves personal and sensitive health data of neonates, requiring strict GDPR compliance, ethical approval, and controlled data access. Commercialization and IP protection also limit open data sharing.
